label: registered S2 run (PROTOCOL Sec. 7.6)
notes: D* is moved to t + s; D_cand moves with it when D_cand = D* in the state (the active candidate is the running job's newest one: coupled_states), otherwise it keeps its value.
States without an active candidate (before the first commit) have no D* and are skipped.
A fresh policy, hence a fresh Q-network utility and overrun window, per network and slack value.

share_admitted = decision epochs whose action lies in A_feas / decision epochs; it does not depend on the utility. The bound of an admitted action is the Eq. 5 sum t + L_pi + L_a + L_commit + R_a + eps.

bypass_rate counts every reason over the choice epochs; bypass_rate_slack is the near-deadline part (a shield margin below B_pi, deterministic), bypass_rate_timing the CPU-timing part (overrun, disabled), which depends on the machine load (S1) and is not a near-deadline effect.

Only D* (and a coupled D_cand) moves. The lease values of the state stay as logged: active_lease_s, cand_lease_s and tau_star_s (network inputs), so D = t_k + H (Eq. 3) does not hold in a moved state. The shield (Eq. 5), A_feas, share_admitted and every Eq. 5 check depend on D*, D_cand and the bounds only; the network's input, hence its choice inside A_feas, sees the logged lease values.

slack_floor: per kappa, the Eq. 5 floors of the slack (an action is admitted only at s > L_pi + L_a + L_commit + R_a + eps) and the grid values at or below every state's floor; per network, by_kappa lists the admitted actions checked per kappa, the grid values that admit nothing and the first admitting slack. Where the floor lies above most of the registered grid, its lower values admit nothing and check no admitted action.
protocol: framelease_v4/PROTOCOL.md Sec. 7.6 (Table II-B stress tests); Eq. 5 / Eq. 8 / Eq. 9 of Sec. 2.4; Sec. 5.7 (budgeted CPU policy execution); Sec. 6.4
